The primitives form a layered framework for detecting and mitigating model drift and bias in football analytics. Calibration drift monitor uses chi-square statistics to detect misalignment between predicted and actual outcomes, ensuring that model reliability remains intact over time. Population stability index leverages KL divergence to quantify shifts in input feature distributions, enabling early detection of data drift. Safe football segment parity enforces fairness by restricting parity checks to football-specific variables such as position, team, and game context, thereby avoiding unintended discrimination based on protected attributes. These operators interact through a shared domain of probabilistic consistency, where each primitive contributes to a holistic view of model integrity. Failure modes include false positives from noisy chi-square tests, spurious drift signals from minor distributional changes, and exclusion of relevant features due to overly restrictive parity rules. Dualities emerge in how statistical measures like PSI mirror information-theoretic concepts, reinforcing the robustness of the system against adversarial perturbations.
